title: Codex-first model routing: fix broken enforcement layer
description: Codex delegation ran at ~3% of delegable work. Root causes: (1) $CODEX_PLUGIN never exported, so the documented readiness check errored and sessions invoked the fallback clause and worked inline; (2) the two routing hooks still encoded the pre-Codex table and ExitPlanMode actively instructed inline Opus builds; (3) hooks lived untracked outside cc-harness with no selftest; (4) no gate fired at the inline-edit moment.
design: Track hooks/ and scripts/ in cc-harness and link them via install.sh. Resolve the plugin root with a semver-aware resolver instead of an unset env var. Add a once-per-session first-edit gate. Every guard gets a falsifiable selftest.
acceptance_criteria: All selftests green at real exit codes; each proven red by mutation; a fresh headless session delegates to Codex instead of working inline.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: semver-aware plugin resolver + wrapper, Codex-first hooks (bd-ready, exitplan, new first-edit gate), install/uninstall symmetry guard, routing-report instrument. All 4 selftests green at real exit codes and each proven red by mutation. Behavioural A/B: pre-fix session worked inline on a false-negative readiness check; post-fix session delegated to codex:codex-rescue.

title: Model routing: stop top-tier escalation from becoming sticky across Codex fix-loop rounds
description: A PR in a now-retired AudioApp worktree burned 13+ consecutive Codex dispatch rounds pinned to gpt-6-astra fixing a hardware-only bug, after one round escalated from gpt-5.6-terra and the escalation never stepped back down for subsequent build/debug rounds. The Model Routing rule has no guidance telling the orchestrator to re-select tier per round instead of carrying an escalation forward by inertia, and codex-dispatch-protocol.md's runaway-signature list only covers a single job's liveness, not a cross-round pattern of repeated top-tier re-dispatch without new diagnostic progress.
acceptance_criteria: global/CLAUDE.md's Model Routing equivalence-table section states that a tier escalation is scoped to the round that needed it, not carried forward; the Mismatch protocol bullet covers per-round reselection in a Codex fix loop, not only ExitPlanMode. rules/codex-dispatch-protocol.md §4's runaway-signature list names repeated top-tier re-dispatch across separate completed job records (same bead/PR, no tier step-down, no new diagnostic input) as a signature requiring cancel-and-rescope. Both edits cross-reference each other. No behavior change outside these two rule files.
close_reason: Landed in PR #65 (https://github.com/gpxl/cc-harness/pull/65). Full 3-round adversarial review, verdict GO, 0 open blockers. Awaiting trusted-pr-merge.sh from a separate checkout.

title: Scan this repo with name-hygiene.sh in the gate, not only its selftest
description: rules/public-surface-hygiene.md claims name-hygiene.sh 'is wired into scripts/verify.sh through the gate list in CLAUDE.md'. Only scripts/name-hygiene-selftest.sh is in that list, and every invocation inside it passes --root pointing at a throwaway fixture repo. Nothing in the gate ever scans cc-harness's own tracked files or commit messages. Run by hand on 2026-09-16 the real scan passes over 102 files, so the tool works and the repo is clean; a leak committed tomorrow would still merge green. This is the repo's own 'instruments must distinguish healthy from not looking' failure in the one place where a miss costs a history rewrite. Reuse the existing tool rather than writing a wrapper: with no arguments it already defaults its root to the repo and exits 1 on a denied token, 2 on a setup error.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/verify.sh runs scripts/name-hygiene.sh against the repo itself and CLAUDE.md's gate section lists it, with the section's wording no longer implying every entry is a selftest; a planted denied token makes bash scripts/verify.sh FAIL at a real exit code; scripts/name-hygiene-selftest.sh gains a row proving the no-argument default root is the repository, with a source mutation that goes red; the rule's enforcement claim is true as written.

title: review-round.sh: resume the recorded reviewer thread by threadId, not by newest-job match
description: Both copies of review-round.sh (cc-harness and the audio app's fork) resume the R1 reviewer only when the newest job record in the plugin state dir carries the R1 threadId. In a Codex-first workflow the fix between rounds is itself a Codex job, so the reviewer is never the newest thread and resume never fires: resumeLast=false on 6 of 6 rounds; the branch-completion rule's 'resume the same reviewer' is dead text. Investigate first: whether codex-companion.mjs task / codex-dispatch.sh can resume a specific thread (a --thread <id> or resume-by-id path; the request today only has resumeLast). If it can, dispatch R2/R3 with the recorded threadId and drop the newest-job check. If it cannot, record that as a plugin limitation in docs/reference/review-round-scripts.md, make the script say 'fresh reviewer: plugin cannot resume by thread' rather than 'thread superseded', and rely on the prior-findings file (cch-q4c sibling) as the continuity mechanism. Either way the selftest must prove which path was taken and that the R1 findings reach the R2 prompt.
acceptance_criteria: Either R2 dispatch carries the R1 threadId and the selftest proves --resume targeted it, or the limitation is documented and the script's message and rule text no longer promise a resume that cannot happen.
close_reason: Closed

title: review-round.sh: refuse R2+ without non-empty acceptance criteria and a prior-findings file
description: Rounds 2-5 of the 6-round branch were dispatched with an empty '## Acceptance criteria' section (the beads named on the branch have no ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA block; 12 of 28 recently closed beads in that project have one) and every R2+ prompt said 'No prior findings file was recorded'. Both placeholders are rendered silently, so a fresh reviewer gets a 7,000-line diff with no definition of done and no history and samples a different subset each round. Change: (1) acceptance_from_bead returning empty (or the fallback text) is exit 2 with a message naming the bead and how to supply criteria (bd update <id> --acceptance, or --bead of a child that has them, or REVIEW_ROUND_ACCEPTANCE); (2) for round >=2, a missing <slug>-r<k>-findings.md for any k<round is exit 2 telling the orchestrator to run --collect (or write the dispositions) first; (3) the deterministic-evidence lookup must read the VERIFY RESULT / CODE QUALITY RESULT lines from wherever the project records them (it printed 'No ... record was found' in all six rounds even when the orchestrator had a PASS stamp) — take a --evidence-file path and fall back to the merge-gate last-summary; missing evidence is a stated gap in the prompt, not a silent placeholder. Add selftest rows for each refusal and a negative control proving each refusal can be green. Also add the acceptance-section requirement to the bead-creation guidance in global/CLAUDE.md Workflow (bd create --acceptance / --validate) so beads used for review carry it.
acceptance_criteria: review-round.sh refuses with a nonzero exit (1, its refusal code; 2 is reserved for usage errors) on empty acceptance criteria and on a missing prior-findings file for R2+; --evidence-file is honoured and a missing evidence file is refused rather than reported as no records; selftest rows for each, every row with a source mutation that goes red; global CLAUDE.md Workflow row says beads that will be reviewed carry --acceptance.
close_reason: Closed

title: review-round.sh: bind the round budget to a scope hash, not the branch slug
description: On the 6-round branch the counter kept incrementing while the reviewed inventory grew from 2 to 27 commits and 856 to 9,339 lines; rounds 2-6 reviewed code round 1 never saw, and the 3-round cap counted the wrong thing. Change: review-round.sh records a scope stamp at round 1 (sha256 of the acceptance text plus the list of non-fix, non-docs commit subjects in base...HEAD). On a later round, if the stamp differs (new feat/refactor commits, changed acceptance), the script refuses to continue the count: it prints REVIEW ROUND: scope changed since round N (<diff of subjects>), resets the counter to 0 for the new stamp (archiving the old counter and findings under <slug>.scope-<hash>/), and requires the acceptance criteria to be restated (via --bead or REVIEW_ROUND_ACCEPTANCE). fix( and test( and docs( commits do not change the stamp. Selftest rows: same stamp increments; a new feat commit resets and refuses without restated acceptance; a fix commit does not reset. Rule text in rules/branch-completion-review.md (The NO-GO loop) gains one sentence: the budget is per scope; new feature commits after R1 restart it with fresh acceptance. Cite the metric in the rule commit: rounds median 3 vs <=2 (rules freeze, 2026-09-05).
acceptance_criteria: review-round.sh writes <slug>.scope at R1; a feat commit after R1 causes the next invocation to refuse with a nonzero exit (1) until --scope-changed declares it, then resets the counter and archives the prior rounds; a fix commit does not move the stamp; selftest proves all three, each with a source mutation that goes red; rule sentence added with metric citation.
close_reason: Closed

title: Review convergence: fewer branch-review rounds per PR
description: Evaluation on 2026-09-16 (post-retrospective ledger 09-07..09-16): rounds per branch 1,3,3,1,1,3,4,2,3,2 plus one open branch at 6 rounds with 15 fix commits of 27; median 3 against a target of <=2. Root causes measured on that branch: (1) the diff grew 856 -> 6,685 -> 9,339 lines across rounds because six beads were built onto one PR, so the per-branch counter counted a moving target; (2) every round was a fresh reviewer (resumeLast=false 6/6, the newest-job resume check can never hold once a fix task runs in between) briefed with an empty acceptance block (beads had no ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA section), 'No prior findings file was recorded' and 'No VERIFY RESULT record was found', so each pass sampled a different subset of the diff; (3) fix tasks ran 3-34 min and re-review was dispatched within ~20 min, with rounds 4 and 5 each finding a defect in the mechanism the round-3 fix introduced. Reviewer output quality and fix-prompt quality were both adequate; the gap is orchestrator->reviewer briefing and implementer self-review before R1. This epic groups the levers. Rule text edits must cite the metric (rounds median 3 vs <=2) per the 2026-09-05 freeze; script changes are unrestricted.
acceptance_criteria: Next five merged PRs across projects using review-round.sh: rounds <=2 median, fix( commits after first review <=3, zero R2+ prompts with an empty acceptance block or missing prior-findings file.
close_reason: All six children landed (PRs #57, #59, #63). IMPLEMENTATION complete; the acceptance criterion is an OUTCOME metric over the next five merged PRs across projects and is therefore unverified — and cannot currently be measured, because cch-8vb records that loop-report.sh reports zero gate runs and zero merge-gate invocations for windows where both occurred. Closing the build, not claiming the outcome.

title: [bug] review-ack-check.sh silently truncates unquoted user_decision and never validates classes=
description:
scripts/review-ack-check.sh is shipped as the PORTABLE bounded-review ack validator for any project's gate, but it is materially weaker than the real gate it is modelled on (AudioApp scripts/merge-gate.sh branch_review_fields_valid). Found 2026-09-08 while recording a branch-review ack for an AudioApp pull request.

Three confirmed defects, all reproducible with bash scripts/review-ack-check.sh '<note>':

1. SILENT TRUNCATION OF user_decision (worst). Input:
     rounds=4 verdict=NO-GO open_blockers=2 classes=3 user_decision=merge anyway
   Output: REVIEW ACK: PASS ... user_decision="merge"  (rc=0)
   It accepts an UNQUOTED multi-word decision and silently drops everything after the first word, so 'merge with disclosure' is recorded as 'merge'. This corrupts the exact field that authorises a merge, and inverts its meaning. AudioApp rejects unquoted user_decision specifically to prevent this; its inline comment says a whitespace-containing choice 'would be silently truncated before it reached the record that authorises a merge'. Our portable checker does the truncation instead of refusing.

2. classes= IS NEVER VALIDATED. 'classes=banana' passes (rc=0). AudioApp requires classes=([1-5])(,[1-5])* — bare risk-class digits. Our checker accepts any string, so the field it is supposed to police is decoration. Note the confusing surface this sits on: AudioApp's merge-gate FAIL message prints the human-readable label ('diff hits risk class(es): 3-check-or-policy-integrity') but the ack must be recorded as classes=3; the portable checker blesses the label form that the real gate then refuses.

3. rounds=0 IS ACCEPTED (rc=0). An ack asserting that ZERO review rounds ran passes. AudioApp requires [1-9][0-9]* .

What it DOES catch correctly (keep these): missing rounds/verdict/open_blockers; verdict not in {GO,NO-GO}; rounds > max_rounds; NO-GO or open_blockers>0 without user_decision.

FIX: bring the field grammar to parity with AudioApp's branch_review_fields_valid — require quoted user_decision="..." and REFUSE the unquoted form rather than truncating it; validate classes as [1-5](,[1-5])*; require rounds>=1.

ALSO: scripts/review-ack-check-selftest.sh currently passes, so it has no negative control for any of the three. Add one per defect — a check that cannot go red on these is why they shipped. See rules/verification-integrity.md.
close_reason: Raw-token validation for all ack fields; 3 original defects + 6 laundering bypasses fixed, negative controls added. Review GO round 2/3. PR #50

title: Every selftest exits 0 when it aborts mid-run — the whole gate can't go red
description: Measured 2026-09-03 across all ten gates (scripts/*selftest*.sh + hooks/selftest.sh): each installs , and cleanup's final command (rm -rf on a temp dir) succeeds, replacing the status of a script dying from set -e/set -u. Injecting an unbound-variable reference immediately after the trap line makes every one of them print the error and exit 0. So a typo, an unset variable, a missing binary, or any abort partway through a suite reads as PASS. This is the exact disease rules/verification-integrity.md exists to prevent, sitting in the apparatus that enforces it — and CLAUDE.md's claim that 'local green means every selftest passes at a real exit code' is not true for the abort class. Note the assertion path is unaffected: a failing assertion still exits 1 correctly. Only aborts are swallowed.
acceptance_criteria: Each selftest's EXIT trap preserves the dying status (capture $? first, exit with it last). Proven by injecting an abort after the trap line in a copy of each and observing a non-zero exit — the same measurement that found this, re-run green.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #39 (d2978cc). All ten gates now fail on abort; verified in three directions (clean=0, real failure=1, injected abort=non-zero).

title: [bug] codex-brokers.sh: unregistered broker defaults to STALE, so a missing state store makes --reap-stale kill LIVE brokers
description: Found by adversarial review of AudioApp PR #6, confirmed on the machine: with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA unset (it is not in any shell profile or settings.json — the harness injects it per-plugin), every broker including ones serving a running job reads verdict=STALE, and --reap-stale SIGKILLs the broker and its codex app-server child. Absence of a registration must never imply safe-to-kill. Fix: verdict UNKNOWN (never reaped) for a broker whose registration was not found but whose cwd exists; STALE only when independently verifiable (cwd missing, or cwd under TMPDIR); and refuse to reap at all when zero broker.json files were discovered.

title: loop-report.sh reports zero gate runs and zero merge-gate invocations where both definitely occurred
description:
Measured 2026-09-17: `bash scripts/loop-report.sh --days 2 --json` summed over the 37 cc-harness transcripts reports gate_runs: 0 and merge_gate_invocations: 0, for a window in which 7 PRs merged and scripts/verify.sh ran many times (each merge went through trusted-pr-merge.sh, which runs the candidate gate).

The detectors are not matching in these transcripts. Zero is the reading that looks like a clean answer, which is exactly the failure rules/verification-integrity.md names: an instrument that cannot see must not report a number indistinguishable from "nothing happened".

This matters more than an ordinary reporting bug because loop-report.sh is the instrument we would use to decide whether the branch-completion review loop is worth its cost. A tool that under-reports gate activity to zero cannot support that decision in either direction.

Also noted while measuring: the script emits no totals row at all, so every caller has to sum the per-transcript objects itself, and `--prs` produced an empty array for the window.
acceptance_criteria:
gate_runs and merge_gate_invocations are non-zero for a window known to contain gate runs and merges, verified against a real captured transcript rather than a hand-written fixture.
A detector that matches nothing reports "unknown" or names what it looked for, rather than 0 (rules/verification-integrity.md: an instrument must distinguish healthy from not-looking).
A selftest row drives a real captured transcript through the detectors and goes red under a source mutation to the match pattern.
Optionally: the report prints a totals row.

title: review-round: delete the coverage extractor instead of patching it a third time
description:
Round 2 of PR #63 raised two MAJORs (MAJOR 4, MAJOR 5), both in the code that extracts the reviewer's COVERAGE map. They are the third and fourth defects in that mechanism in as many rounds:

- R1 MAJOR 1: the extractor ended the block on the first blank line while still printing the COVERAGE header, so a map with a blank line read as "nobody recorded a gap".
- (found while building R2's own prompt): a not-traced= line quoted inside a fenced block in a findings file was carried forward as a real target.
- R2 MAJOR 4: the fence guard was added to collect_not_traced (the findings-file reader) but not to final_findings_from_log (the job-log reader), which strips the fence markers first. So the default --collect path still flattens a quoted example into a recorded gap.
- R2 MAJOR 5: removing the blank-line terminator left the block ending only on a severity or verdict line, so a report placing ### UNVERIFIED after the map has that whole section absorbed into not-traced=.

THE REVIEWER'S REQUIRED FIX was to teach final_findings_from_log the same fence rule and widen the terminator set. That is a third patch to a mechanism that has produced a defect every round, which templates/review-fix-round.md says is itself the finding.

THE STRUCTURAL ALTERNATIVE, and why it is smaller: review-round.sh:684 already inlines each prior findings file VERBATIM into the next round's prompt, COVERAGE map included. Line 685 then re-parses that same file with awk to build a separate not-traced section appended at :788. The extractor's only job is to restate text the prompt already carries. Deleting it removes all four defect classes at once and roughly 60 lines of parsing.

Decide between the two with the evidence above; do not silently pick the patch because it is what the reviewer wrote.
acceptance_criteria:
Either (a) the extractor is deleted: collect_not_traced, the coverage branch of final_findings_from_log, and prior_not_traced/coverage_targets are gone; the round-N prompt instead carries a static instruction telling the reviewer that each inlined prior findings file ends with a COVERAGE map and to spend its budget on that map's not-traced= line first; the selftest rows that pinned the extractor's parsing are deleted rather than rewritten; and a selftest row proves the static instruction reaches the dispatched prompt.
OR (b) the patch is taken and BOTH MAJOR 4 and MAJOR 5 are closed, each with a selftest row that drives a real job log through --collect (not a hand-written findings file) and a source mutation proving the row goes red.
Whichever is chosen, the reasoning is recorded in the commit body.

title: Routing check: no selftest row proves managed link drift is reported

title: Check whether a rename out of a high-risk path escapes the merge filter
description: scripts/trusted-pr-merge.sh classifies a pull request from the changed-path list returned by the GraphQL files connection, which exposes the new path and no previous path. If a rename reports only the destination, moving a file OUT of rules/, scripts/ or another covered directory would not trigger the high-risk classification, and deleting a check by renaming it elsewhere would merge without a review acknowledgement. Raised as unverified by round 2 of the review on feat/harness-self-validation: settling it needs a live GitHub response for a renaming pull request, which that branch had no way to obtain.
acceptance_criteria: The behaviour is established against a real GitHub API response for a pull request that renames a file out of a covered directory; if the previous path is absent from the classification input, the wrapper is changed to obtain it and treat a rename out of a covered path as high risk, with a selftest row driven by a recorded payload and a source mutation that goes red; if the previous path is already present, the finding is recorded as not applicable with the evidence.

title: Scan pull-request titles for denied names before merge

title: Require a valid review acknowledgement before merging a review-triggering PR

On 2026-09-16 PR #57 merged exactly that way: the review really had returned GO with zero blockers, and no machine confirmed it. scripts/trusted-pr-merge.sh already classifies PRs host-side and already carries a high_risk_path set covering rules/, agents/ and CLAUDE.md, so the acknowledgement requirement belongs there, validated with the TRUSTED copy of review-ack-check.sh and never one from the candidate checkout.
acceptance_criteria: trusted-pr-merge.sh holds a PR that touches a review-triggering path unless its body carries an acknowledgement that review-ack-check.sh accepts, reporting a distinct stable reason; the acknowledgement is validated with the trusted harness copy of the checker, never the candidate's; a PR touching no review-triggering path is unaffected; selftest rows cover the held case, the accepted case, a malformed acknowledgement and the untouched case, each with a source mutation that goes red.

title: Machine-check that every rule is indexed in global/CLAUDE.md

An unindexed rule fails silently and invisibly: the file is present, readable and simply never loaded, which is the worst shape a failure can take. Precedent for a doc-consistency check in the gate already exists in scripts/verify-selftest.sh, which compares verify.sh's default list against the gate list written in CLAUDE.md.
acceptance_criteria: A check in the gate fails when a file in rules/ has no entry in the [Rules] index of global/CLAUDE.md, and fails when an index entry names a rule file that does not exist; both directions have a negative control that goes red; the check reports which rule or entry is at fault by name.

title: review-round.sh: reject stale gate evidence by tree hash

It does not check that the recorded tree= still matches the working tree, so a stale record from before the last edit reads to the reviewer as current gate evidence. That is the same class the branch exists to remove: an instrument that cannot tell fresh from stale reporting healthy. Raised as a BEAD by round 1 of the branch review on feat/review-convergence-round-script; deliberately not fixed there to keep the reviewed scope fixed.
acceptance_criteria: review-round.sh compares each carried record's tree= against the stamp of the current working tree; a record whose tree= does not match is either refused by name or carried with an explicit stale marker in the prompt; a selftest row proves the stale case is distinguished from the fresh one, with a source mutation that goes red.

title: Reviewer output contract: require a coverage map so R2+ targets gaps instead of resampling

Each fresh reviewer samples a different subset of a large diff and nothing carries the gaps forward. Selftest: a captured real log with a COVERAGE block round-trips into the r2 prompt; a log without one produces a stated 'no coverage map recorded' line, not a silent omission (cch-aif's bold-bullet extraction gap is adjacent; fix together if cheap).
acceptance_criteria: Prompt contract includes COVERAGE; --collect extracts it; R2 prompt inlines not-traced items as targets; selftest proves the round-trip on a real captured sample.

Change: add a fix-round prompt template (templates/review-fix-round.md, referenced from rules/branch-completion-review.md 'The NO-GO loop') with three mandatory sections: (1) verbatim findings with dispositions; (2) SIBLINGS: for each finding, search the whole branch diff for the same failure class and fix or list every instance; (3) STRUCTURE: if two or more rounds have found defects in one mechanism, say whether it needs restructuring rather than a fourth patch and propose it (the round-6 prompt did this and got GO in one minute). Forbid budget-pressure lines; the budget is the orchestrator's problem. Add the retrospective's ratchet counterexample (a fix that reintroduced round 1's race) as the standing example. Rule edit cites the metric.

title: Codex build mailbox: let a sandboxed Codex turn get a real build/test result
description: Codex cannot run swift build or scripts/test.sh inside its sandbox (nested Seatbelt kills swift-plugin-server, so every @State/@Observable macro site fails to expand). Every AudioApp handoff therefore returns UNVERIFIED code, and the orchestrator pays Claude tokens for a build -> collect errors -> --resume loop, repeatedly, for mistakes Codex would have caught itself if it could compile. A mailbox lets a sandboxed turn request a command run OUTSIDE the sandbox and read the result back, collapsing N Claude round trips into one. SECURITY: this is deliberately a hole in the sandbox, so the runner must execute only an allowlisted set of commands in a fixed workspace, never arbitrary text from the request.
design: Three parts: (1) a detached host-side runner that polls a mailbox dir; (2) a request/response file protocol; (3) a client the Codex prompt calls. Follows the codex-wait.sh precedent for detached polling. Load-bearing assumption to probe FIRST: can a sandboxed Codex turn write a request and block for a reply within one turn, while Claude is itself blocked on that task?
acceptance_criteria: A Codex task that cannot compile can obtain a real compiler error list from outside its sandbox within one turn; the runner refuses any command not on the allowlist, proven by a negative control; no path lets request content reach a shell as code.
notes: BLOCKED after adversarial review + direct verification. Two sandbox escapes reproduced on-machine (arbitrary host-file overwrite via a caller-planted log symlink; killing any same-user process via a forged runner.pid). Attempted fix committed as b66aca7 on claude/codex-build-mailbox (PR #38, now human/hold) but NOT ready: (1) start/status/stop all crash under bash 3.2 — 'local a=$1 b=$a/x' expands before assigning; (2) the forged-PID assertion is vacuously green because stop crashes before reaching the guard, and the suite never invokes start/status at all; (3) the fix assumes $TMPDIR is host-private, which is likely false for a workspace-write sandbox — UNVERIFIED and must be settled first; (4) unaddressed: mv of a consumed request to req-<id>.json.done follows a caller-planted symlink to a directory = write-anywhere primitive with caller-chosen content. Root cause is structural: the host trusts a directory the untrusted party writes. Next attempt: state under $HOME (not sandbox-writable), no PID file (runner holds an flock), refuse any delivery destination that exists as a symlink or directory. FIRST decide whether the feature is worth it at all — the orchestrator polling for a request file and running swift build itself buys the same token saving with zero host-side trust.

title: review-round-selftest: make make_mutant assert that its substitution applied
description: make_mutant() seds a copy of the tool but never checks that the pattern matched. A mutation row whose sed silently no-ops, or that kills the script before dispatch, can read as red for the wrong reason — every row that asserts 'goes red' accepts rc != 0 or a missing output file. All current patterns were hand-verified to match exactly one line, but nothing keeps that true. Fix: have make_mutant diff the mutant against the source and fail loudly when they are identical. Found in the PR #59 branch-completion review (round 1, NIT).
acceptance_criteria: make_mutant fails the suite when its sed changes nothing; all existing rows still pass.

title: review-round: collect the body of a bullet-style finding, not just its first line
description: final_findings_from_log() prints only the matching line. In bullet form (- **BLOCKER — f:10** ...) the title and body share a line, so a wrapped finding is collected truncated mid-sentence: the shipped fixture yields '... deletes from the map but not from the'. The prior-findings file is the only continuity a fresh round-2 reviewer gets, so it now carries dangling clauses. Fix: after a matched bullet, keep collecting indented non-blank continuation lines until the next blank line or next bullet. Found in the PR #59 branch-completion review (round 1, MINOR).
acceptance_criteria: A wrapped bullet finding is collected whole, up to the next blank line or bullet; heading-style findings are unaffected; a selftest row covers a wrapped bullet with a source mutation that goes red.

title: review-round.sh: name which half of the scope stamp moved
description: The scope-change refusal prints 'the reviewed scope changed since round N' plus the commit subject list, but the stamp is a digest of the acceptance text AND the subjects. A typo fix in a bead's acceptance therefore refuses with a subject list identical to round 1's, and the only sanctioned remedy restarts the budget at 1 — so a wording edit silently buys three more rounds and the operator cannot see why. Raised as a BEAD by round 2 of the review on feat/review-convergence-round-script; kept off that branch to hold its reviewed scope fixed.
acceptance_criteria: review-round.sh records the acceptance digest separately from the commit-subject digest and the refusal names which component moved; a change confined to the acceptance text is distinguishable from new commits, and the decision on whether it should reset the counter at all is made explicitly and documented; selftest rows cover both components moving independently, each with a source mutation that goes red.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add a grep-able budget-language check for written fix prompts
description: templates/review-fix-round.md forbids telling an implementation task how much review budget is left, but nothing checks a prompt actually written from it. Orchestrators that materialise a fix prompt to a file should be able to run one check that fails on 'last round', 'last allowed', 'round N of N' and similar countdown phrasing, in the style of scripts/name-hygiene.sh. Split out of cch-q4c.6, whose branch shipped the template and the rule wiring but no such check; the branch was under review at the time and growing its reviewed scope was the exact failure mode the epic exists to remove.
acceptance_criteria: A script fails, naming the offending line, on a prompt file containing remaining-budget or countdown phrasing, and passes a prompt written from templates/review-fix-round.md; a selftest covers both directions with a source mutation that goes red; the script is listed in the CLAUDE.md gate list if it is wired into scripts/verify.sh.

title: review-round-selftest: guard the next-round late-threadId resolution path
description: Source mutation 'delayed_thread_id=""' (the round-N+1 path that resolves a threadId recorded late from the previous round's job record) leaves review-round-selftest.sh green. Consequence if that path breaks: a late thread id degrades round 2 to a fresh reviewer instead of a resume — a quality degradation, not an integrity hole. Add a row that records a job with an empty thread at round 1, populates the job record afterwards, and asserts round 2 resumes that thread; prove it red with the mutation above. title: codex-dispatch-protocol: state that background workers/brokers are already setsid-detached; foreground is the only path a harness kill reaches
description: Measured 2026-09-02: harness timeout kills the Bash call's process group (plain child dead), a Node detached:true child (own session, ppid 1) survives. The plugin's spawnDetachedTaskWorker and spawnBrokerProcess both use detached:true, so no extra setsid wrapper is needed for --background; wrapping a FOREGROUND task in setsid would detach a worker no record tracks. Add this to the rule so nobody adds redundant or harmful setsid trickery.

title: Investigate transient Codex brokers spawned with a garbage --cwd (text from a Bash tool call)
description: Seen twice on 2026-09-01 while running codex-brokers-selftest from a AudioApp session: an app-server-broker.mjs serve process appeared with --cwd '%s' and later with --cwd set to a chunk of the Bash tool call's own text; each self-terminated within a minute. No cc-harness hook invokes codex-companion (checked bd-ready-model-routing.sh, first-edit-codex-gate.sh, exitplan-model-routing.sh); plugin hooks are SessionStart/End/Stop only. Reproduce with codex-brokers.sh in a loop while a Bash call containing the literal '--cwd %s' runs; check the plugin's stop-review-gate-hook and any peer session's hooks. Harmless (STALE verdict, self-exits) but is exactly the ghost-state the dispatch protocol exists to prevent.

title: trusted-pr-merge: match each renamed file's previous path instead of counting them
description: load_pr() accepts the REST previous-path list when its length is at least the RENAMED count. That proves enough paths came back, not that each renamed file's old path is among them: REST also sets previous_filename for status=copied, so a copy could pad the count for a rename whose old path is missing. No real GitHub response was found where a RENAMED file lacks previous_filename, so this is theoretical and fail-closed in the direction that matters. Raised UNVERIFIED by round 2 of the review on PR #61.
acceptance_criteria: Each RENAMED file's previous path is matched by its new path rather than inferred from a count; a selftest row drives a payload where a copy pads the count and asserts the rename is still refused, with a source mutation that goes red.

title: review-round: anchor the tree= match to the first occurrence on a record line
description: evidence_records() reads the recorded tree with a greedy '.*(^|[[:space:]])tree=([0-9a-f]+).*', which takes the LAST tree= on the line. A record that mentions a second tree hash after the recorded one would be graded against the later value and could read as fresh while stale. No current producer emits that, but it is the only path found by which a stale record reads fresh. Found in the PR #59 branch-completion review (round 1, NIT).
acceptance_criteria: The first tree= on a record line is the one compared; a selftest row feeds a line with two tree= fields and asserts the first wins, with a source mutation that goes red.
